HOUSE COURTS, NEW DELHI
Raghunandan SaranAshok Saran (HUF),
40­42, Janpath, New Delhi,
through its Karta Ashok Saran
R/o flat No:9, 40­42, Janpath, New Delhi           .....Petitioner
Versus
1. National Insurance Co. Ltd. Division No:1,
4, Peareylal Bldg, 42­Janpath, New Delhi­110001
2. Sh. M.L. Sharma  S/o Kundan Lal
R/o 40­42, Janpath, New Delhi­110001
3. Roop Sharma S/o M.L. Sharma
R/o 40­42, Janpath, New Delhi­110001
4. Rajiv Nanda S/o Om Prakash Nanda,
R/o 40­42, Janpath, New Delhi­110001
PETITION UNDER SECTION 14(1)(B) OF DELHI RENT CONTROL
DATE OF INSTITUTION OF THE PETITION
EC No:E­13/08/09, Raghunandan Saran Ashok Saran (HUF)  Vs. National
Insurance Co. Ltd.
DATE OF FINAL ARGUMENT/CLARIFICATION
DATE OF FINAL JUDGMENT
JUDGMENT

1. Petitioner has filed the present petition u/s 14(1)(b) of Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 against the respondents for eviction from the tenanted premises comprises of Second Floor, Flat No:2, bearing Municipal No:
> 40/6, of premises on third floor bearing Municipal No:40/16 and of premises on Second Floor, Flat No:3, bearing Municipal No:40/7 ( Portion of 40­42, Janpath, New Delhi).

2. It is stated by the petitioner that he is the landlord of the aforesaid premises and National Insurance Co. Ltd. is the tenant regarding aforesaid premises. It is averred by the petitioner that originally premises were leased to New Zealand Insurance Co. Ltd. w.e.f. 1940 which company subsequently was nationalized by Government of India and subsumed under National Insurance Company Limited.

It is further averred by the petitioner that total rate of rent regarding tenanted premises since 1940 is Rs.283/­ It is stated by the petitioner that portion of the suit premises has been and is in exclusive possession of Sh. M.L Sharma , Roop Sharma and Rajiv Handa being given without written consent of the landlord.
EC No:E­13/08/09, Raghunandan Saran Ashok Saran (HUF) Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd.

3. Petitioner stated that he has sought eviction of tenant on the ground that tenant has sublet, assigned or otherwise parted with possession of a part of the premises, without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord, to one M. L. Sharma, to one Roop Sharma and to one Rajiv Handa who have been and are in exclusive possession of portion of the premises bearing Municipal No:40/16.

4. Written statement filed on behalf of the respondent No:1. It is denied by the defendant No:1 that portion of the suit premises has been in exclusive possession of M.L.Sharma, Roop Sharma and Rajiv Handa. It is further stated that Defendant No:1 has absolutely no concerned with the aforesaid persons.

Defendant No:1 further denied that they have sublet, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of a part of premises without obtaining the consent in writing of landlord to M.L.Sharma, Roop Sharma and Rajiv Handa who have been and are in exclusive possession of portion of premises bearing No:40/16. Defendant No:1 stated that he is in possession of the premises in its entirely and the portion of subletting etc. does not arise at all.
Defendant No:1 prayed for dismissal of the petition of the petitioner with costs.

5. Defendant No:2 to 4 have also filed their written statement. It is stated that plaintiff has not come to the court with clean hands and EC No:E­13/08/09, Raghunandan Saran Ashok Saran (HUF) Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd.

suppressed material facts as it is very much in the knowledge of the petitioner that respondent No:2 was in the employment of the Respondent No:1 since 1952 and therefore, the respondent No:2 was provided with the accommodation situated at 3rd Floor of property No:40/16, Pyare Lal Building, Janpath, New Delhi.

It is submitted that previously the company was deducting the amount on account of provision of the premises from the salary of the respondent No:2 but later on with the change of management, the company stopped deducting any amount from the salary of the respondent No:2 and treated as free accommodation and even after the retirement of the respondent No:2 in 1978 the company never asked for the vacation of the premises in dispute from the respondent and since then the respondent No:2 is residing there and there is no question of subletting to him.

It is denied by the defendants No:2 to 4 that portion of the premises was given to the them without any written consent of the landlord. It is stated that respondent No:3 Roop sharma is the con of the respondent No:2 and Sh. Rajeev Nanda­respondent No:4 is the son­in­law of the respondent No:2 and they are not staying permanently in the suit premises and they being the close relative of the respondent No:2 frequently visiting the respondent No:2, otherwise said Sh. Roop Sharma and Sh.
Rajeev Nanda have nothing to do with the EC No:E­13/08/09, Raghunandan Saran Ashok Saran (HUF) Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd.
premises in question.

6. Petitioner Ashok Saran filed his evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex. P­1 bearing his signature at point A and B and reiterated the contents of his main petition. Site plan showing the various portions of property bearing No:40­40, Janpath, New Delhi , comprising suit premises is Ex. PW1/1. Notice u/o XII rule 4 CPC dt.22­2­2006 sent to respondent No:1 through Registered A/D is Ex. PW1/2, its A/D card is Ex. PW1/3.

Another notice under order XII rule 8 CPC r/w section 66 of Indian Evidence Act dt.31­8­2001 is Ex.PW1/4 and its A/D card and its copy is Ex. PW1/5 & Ex. PW1/6, postal receipt is Ex. PW1/7. Photocopy of the MTNL telephone Director 1999 Volume II Page 1704 is Ex. PW1/9.

During his cross examination by the ld. Counsel for the respondent No:1, PW1 Ashok Saran stated that he can not say whether any lease deed or written document was executed when the property in question was let out. PW1 stated that he was not the Karta of the petitioner in 1940 when the tenancy was created and even he was not present at the time of creation of tenancy. He further stated that he is not aware whether any written agreement for tenancy was executed or not.
PW1 stated that 40/6,40/7 and 40/16 are located in Piare Lal Building built on two plots EC No:E­13/08/09, Raghunandan Saran Ashok Saran (HUF) Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd.

bearing No:40 & 42. PW1 denied the suggestion that second floor is not a part of the premises No:40/16 as shown in blue colour in the site plan Ex. PW1/1. PW1 admitted that flat No:2 and 3 are being used for residential purposes. PW1 voluntarily deposed that it was used for residential purposes only after petition u/s 14(1)(k) of DRC Act were initiated and user was changed from commercial to residential and only second floor portion was used for office of New Zealand Insurance Company.

PW1 stated that portion shown in blue colour in Ex. PW1/1 was always used for residential purposes but he is not aware of the fact that who was in the possession of blue portion in 1972. PW2 stated that he does not know respondent No:2 personally and whether he has been retired from New Zealand Insurance Company. PW1 denied the suggestion that there is no subletting or parting with the possession by respondent No:1.
PW1 further denied that Ex.PW1/8 and PW1/9 does not indicate as to the respondent No:2 is in possession of which portion of property No:40/16.
No other witness has been examined by the petitioner and petitioner closed his evidence on 24­05­2008.

7. Respondent No:1 examined Sh. Ram Niwas, Deputy manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd as RW1 and filed his evidence by way of EC No:E­13/08/09, Raghunandan Saran Ashok Saran (HUF) Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd.

affidavit which is Ex. R1W­1/A. It is deposed by R1W1 Sh. Ram Niwas that tenanted premises was let out by the petitioner to M/s New Zealand Insurance Co Ltd. In 1940 which company stood transferred to and vested in the respondent No:1 company copy vide notification dt.1­1­1973 is Ex. R1. R1W1 Sh. Ram Niwas. R1W1 Sh.

Ram Niwas deposed that respondent No:2 was in the employment of the said M/s New Zealand Insurance Company and on account of his employment with the said company, he was permitted user of a portion of the said property by the said company even before 1972. R1W1 Sh. Ram Niwas deposed that defendant No:1 has never sublet, assigned or otherwise parted with possession of any portion of the tenanted premises to defendant No:2 to 8 or to any other person.

R1W1 Sh. Ram Niwas was cross examined by the petitioner at length. During his cross examination R1W1 Sh. Ram Niwas stated that he never worked in New Zealand Insurance Company and paragraph No:1 of his affidavit is on the basis of personal knowledge and remaining paragraphs no:2 to 9 are based on the office record. R1W1 Sh. Ram Niwas stated that he was not present when the premises was taken on rent and also when Respondent No:2 got his employment with the New Zealand Insurance Co.
During the cross examination of R1W1 Sh. Ram EC No:E­13/08/09, Raghunandan Saran Ashok Saran (HUF) Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd.

Niwas, attendance register and leave register of the respondent No:1 w.e.f. 1976 to 1979, filed on behalf of the respondent No:1 has been marked as R­1 , running on page 209 to page 667. R1W1 Sh. Ram Niwas admitted that name of Sh. M.L. Sharma is not mentioned in the list mark R­1. He further stated that he has no personal knowledge in respect of employment of Sh. M.L. Sharma.

Respondent No:1 also examined Sh. Dinesh Kumar Sharma as RW2 and filed his evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex.RW2/A. RW2 Sh. Dinesh Kumar Sharma has deposed on the same line as deposed by R1W1 Sh. Ram Niwas. RW2 Sh. Dinesh Kumar Sharma deposed that form dt.28­6­1974 submitted by M.L. Sharma to respondent No:1 company is Ex. RW2/1 and form for fixation new scales and basis details/data of Mr. M.L. Sharma/respondent No:2 are Ex. RW2/2 and Ex.
RW2/3 and his salary calculation sheet for January, 1973 to June 1974 is Ex. RW2/4.

During his cross examination RW2 Sh. Dinesh Kumar Sharma stated that he was never an employee of New Zealand Insurance Company and he has no personal knowledge regarding the present case and he deposed on the basis of official records. RW2 Sh. Dinesh Kumar Sharma stated that facts mentioned in the para 6 of his affidavit are not EC No:E­13/08/09, Raghunandan Saran Ashok Saran (HUF) Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd.

based on document. He further stated that M.L. Sharma was employee of the respondent and he was permitted only to reside in the premises as employee. During cross examination of RW2 Sh. Dinesh Kumar Sharma the petitioner read over the contents of the para 16 of the WS of respondent No:1 wherein it is written that Sh. M.L. Sharma has no connection with the respondent No:1. RW2 Sh. Dinesh Kumar Sharma stated that what is written in the written statement of the defendant No:1 is correct. RW2 Sh.
Dinesh Kumar Sharma stated that he does not know whether after the retirement Mr. M.L. Sharma was allowed to reside at 40/16.

Mrs. Madhu Sharma who is the daughter of the respondent No:2 Sh. M.L. Sharma has been examined as RW3. RW3 Ms. Madhu Sharma deposed that his father Sh. M.L. Sharma expired on 17­3­2007 and he left behind Smt. Prem Lata Sharma (Wife of deceased) and Sh. Roop Sharma (Son of deceased). RW3 Ms. Madhu Sharma further deposed that her father was working as Driver with Newzealand Insurance Company and her father continued to work with National Insurance Company as driver.

During her cross examination RW3 Ms. Madhu Sharma stated that her father was not employed anywhere in 1998­1999. RW3 Ms. Madhu Sharma admitted that her father expired at 40/16, 42 Janpath, New Delhi. EC No:E­13/08/09, Raghunandan Saran Ashok Saran (HUF) Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd.
She further deposed that Rajiv Nanda is her husband.
No other witness has been examined on behalf of the respondent No:1 and respondent evidence was closed on 2­9­2009.
